newsitem.title: ITALY: INA, BNL offer 60 bln lire for BancoNapoli - paper.
newsitem.headline: INA, BNL offer 60 bln lire for BancoNapoli - paper.

text.p: Italian insurer INA and Banca Nazionale del Lavoro have bid 60 billion lire ($39 million) for the 60 percent stake being offered in southern bank Banco di Napoli, financial daily Il Sole 24 Ore reported on Tuesday.
Recently privatised INA and Treasury-controlled BNL have presented a joint bid for loss-making Banco di Napoli, which the Treasury rescued from collapse earlier this year.

The Treasury, which last week went ahead with a two trillion lire capital increase for the troubled Neapolitan bank, has also received an offer from state-owned credit institute Mediocredito Centrale.
However, all indications point to INA-BNL being successful.

"We will continue the restructuring of the banking system, of Banco di Napoli and BNL, with (their) privatisations in which INA...will be the core-shareholder," Prime Minister Romano Prodi told French newspaper Les Echos on Monday.
Offers for the Banco di Napoli stake had to be placed by the end of last week and the Treasury must announce which group has made the highest bid by January 20.
Il Sole, quoting "reliable" sources, said BNL and INA had valued Banco di Napoli at just 100 billion lire, making the tranche on offer worth some 60 billion lire.

The Treasury has promised to set up a rump company to take on much of Banco di Napoli's huge stock of bad loans but the eventual buyer of the bank will have to cover its 1996 losses, put at some 1.7 trillion lire.
INA said in a statement on Monday that if its bid for Banco di Napoli were successful it would take 51 percent of the firm and BNL 49 percent.
The Treasury has promised to sell the remaining 40 percent of Banco di Napoli rapidly.
